classification.difficultyReason: Combines substitution, reading vertex form, sketching and interpreting intercept counts.

content.prompt:
For each parabola:

i determine the $y$-intercept

ii write down the axis of symmetry and the vertex

iii sketch the parabola

iv determine from the sketch whether the parabola has no $x$-intercepts, one $x$-intercept or two $x$-intercepts

answer.short: $y$-intercept $3$; axis $x=0$; vertex $(0,3)$; no $x$-intercepts. Sketch shown in panel a.
answer.worked: When $x=0$, $y=0^2+3=3$. The form $y=(x-0)^2+3$ gives axis $x=0$ and vertex $(0,3)$. The parabola opens upwards and has minimum value $3>0$, so it has no $x$-intercepts.

spec.description: Individual panel a. Nine labelled solution sketches in source order. Each panel shows the vertex, y-intercept and dashed axis of symmetry; coordinates use independent horizontal and vertical scales.

answer.short: $y$-intercept $-7$; axis $x=0$; vertex $(0,-7)$; two $x$-intercepts. Sketch shown in panel b.
answer.worked: When $x=0$, $y=0^2-7=-7$. The form $y=(x-0)^2-7$ gives axis $x=0$ and vertex $(0,-7)$. The parabola opens upwards with its vertex below the $x$-axis, so its sketch crosses that axis twice.

spec.description: Individual panel b. Nine labelled solution sketches in source order. Each panel shows the vertex, y-intercept and dashed axis of symmetry; coordinates use independent horizontal and vertical scales.

answer.short: $y$-intercept $8$; axis $x=2$; vertex $(2,4)$; no $x$-intercepts. Sketch shown in panel c.
answer.worked: When $x=0$, $y=(-2)^2+4=8$. Vertex form gives axis $x=2$ and vertex $(2,4)$. The parabola opens upwards and has minimum value $4>0$, so it has no $x$-intercepts.

spec.description: Individual panel c. Nine labelled solution sketches in source order. Each panel shows the vertex, y-intercept and dashed axis of symmetry; coordinates use independent horizontal and vertical scales.

answer.short: $y$-intercept $2$; axis $x=3$; vertex $(3,-7)$; two $x$-intercepts. Sketch shown in panel d.
answer.worked: When $x=0$, $y=(-3)^2-7=2$. Vertex form gives axis $x=3$ and vertex $(3,-7)$. The parabola opens upwards with its vertex below the $x$-axis, so its sketch crosses that axis twice.

spec.description: Individual panel d. Nine labelled solution sketches in source order. Each panel shows the vertex, y-intercept and dashed axis of symmetry; coordinates use independent horizontal and vertical scales.

answer.short: $y$-intercept $25$; axis $x=-5$; vertex $(-5,0)$; one $x$-intercept. Sketch shown in panel e.
answer.worked: When $x=0$, $y=5^2=25$. The form $y=(x-(-5))^2+0$ gives axis $x=-5$ and vertex $(-5,0)$. The parabola opens upwards and touches the $x$-axis at its vertex, giving one $x$-intercept.

spec.description: Individual panel e. Nine labelled solution sketches in source order. Each panel shows the vertex, y-intercept and dashed axis of symmetry; coordinates use independent horizontal and vertical scales.

answer.short: $y$-intercept $48$; axis $x=7$; vertex $(7,-1)$; two $x$-intercepts. Sketch shown in panel f.
answer.worked: When $x=0$, $y=(-7)^2-1=48$. Vertex form gives axis $x=7$ and vertex $(7,-1)$. The parabola opens upwards with its vertex below the $x$-axis, so its sketch crosses that axis twice.

spec.description: Individual panel f. Nine labelled solution sketches in source order. Each panel shows the vertex, y-intercept and dashed axis of symmetry; coordinates use independent horizontal and vertical scales.

answer.short: $y$-intercept $-9$; axis $x=3$; vertex $(3,0)$; one $x$-intercept. Sketch shown in panel g.
answer.worked: When $x=0$, $y=-(-3)^2=-9$. Vertex form gives axis $x=3$ and vertex $(3,0)$. The parabola opens downwards and touches the $x$-axis at its vertex, giving one $x$-intercept.

spec.description: Individual panel g. Nine labelled solution sketches in source order. Each panel shows the vertex, y-intercept and dashed axis of symmetry; coordinates use independent horizontal and vertical scales.

answer.short: $y$-intercept $4$; axis $x=-1$; vertex $(-1,5)$; two $x$-intercepts. Sketch shown in panel h.
answer.worked: When $x=0$, $y=-(1)^2+5=4$. Vertex form gives axis $x=-1$ and vertex $(-1,5)$. The parabola opens downwards with its vertex above the $x$-axis, so its sketch crosses that axis twice.

spec.description: Individual panel h. Nine labelled solution sketches in source order. Each panel shows the vertex, y-intercept and dashed axis of symmetry; coordinates use independent horizontal and vertical scales.

answer.short: $y$-intercept $-5$; axis $x=2$; vertex $(2,-1)$; no $x$-intercepts. Sketch shown in panel i.
answer.worked: When $x=0$, $y=-(-2)^2-1=-5$. Vertex form gives axis $x=2$ and vertex $(2,-1)$. The parabola opens downwards and has maximum value $-1<0$, so it has no $x$-intercepts.
